entry.title: Social Summary: October 09, 2026
entry.summary:
Government-industry science funding and Anthropic's sweeping security expansion dominated the day, while Francois Chollet's capex-vs-progress analysis framed growing worries about AI's economic sustainability.

  • Francois Chollet argued AI progress is exponential while capital expenditure grows super-exponentially, warning the industry must generate matching returns — the most-discussed original analysis
  • Anthropic launched the Cyber Mission, OSS Scanner, and a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program in a coordinated security push; Clement Delangue separately urged public release of AI agent attack/defense traces
  • The White House announced $6B+ in science initiatives with $2.4B in pledged compute; Demis Hassabis and Anthropic each committed $150M to the Genesis Mission
  • LMArena raised a $200M Series B at a $3.1B valuation and launched an Alignment Index; CEO Anastasios Angelopoulos reported misalignment in 50%+ of conversations past 20 turns
  • levelsio documented thousands of bots scraping new X links within seconds, an original investigation that drew massive engagement
  • AI-and-mathematics tensions ran high: Yann LeCun proclaimed a new era for math, while the Association for Human Mathematics criticized OpenAI's 722-paper release; a new cube-packing record surfaced via AI methods
  • Nick Bostrom argued a prolonged AI pause could cost more lives than it saves, a contrarian take that sparked debate
  • Product news: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 debuted #4 on image leaderboards at half the price; Gemini was positioned as a universal work agent; Anthropic added monthly API credits to Max and Team plans

entry.title: Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI cape...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that while most measures of AI progress fit an exponential curve from 2023-2026, AI capital expenditure has grown slightly super-exponentially (its growth rate is itself accelerating). Framing AI as a system converting investment into progress, he concludes the response is sub-linear, and warns that continued super-exponential external investment is unsustainable — the industry must generate matching exponential profits to close the resource loop and sustain progress.

entry.title: Excited to support the Genesis Mission @WhiteHouse @ENERGY and Director @mkratsios47 with $150M in i...
entry.summary: Demis Hassabis announces DeepMind support for the US Genesis Mission initiative involving the White House and Department of Energy, with $150M in investments and a stated interest in collaborating on the future of science.

LeCun, in French, argues that AI-driven automation of formal proof opens a new era for mathematics in which human effort shifts toward new concepts, abstractions, definitions, and conjectures, offering the metaphor that the invention of boats reduced the importance of swimming while enabling the discovery of new lands.

entry.title: We’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a new effort to secure critical infrastructure and open...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces the launch of the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a new initiative aimed at securing critical infrastructure and open-source software, with a link to the full announcement.

entry.title: I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on...
entry.summary: levelsio documents an investigation, aided by Claude analysis, showing thousands of bots crawl new links posted on X within seconds: a test URL buried in a reply thread attracted thousands of crawlers in 8 seconds, including a military intelligence firm selling breaking-news alerts to newsrooms, banks and governments, and a social media monitoring company; X's own Twitterbot hits instantly.

entry.title: Huge day. $200M Series B at a $3.1B valuation for @arena and the release of our Alignment Index. I a...
entry.summary: The author, apparently an Arena leader, announces a $200M Series B at a $3.1B valuation for LMArena (@arena) along with the launch of an Alignment Index for evaluating AI under real-world conditions. The ~90-person team is hiring across ML, product, engineering, design, marketing, and BD.

entry.title: We're deepening our commitment to scientific research and technological discovery by committing $150...
entry.summary: Anthropic commits $150 million to the Genesis Mission to deepen its support of scientific research and technological discovery, and will make Claude and technical support available to more than 15 federal agencies.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Google just turned Gemini into one universal agent for work, and it can use Ant...
entry.summary: MTS Live explains Google's move to turn Gemini into a universal work agent with a single interface that can chat, autonomously pursue objectives, generate media, and write and run code. It integrates with Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Microsoft 365 and Slack, can run tasks for hours or days in the cloud, supports coworker agents with their own email, calendar and permissions, and can also use Anthropic's Claude.

entry.title: Monthly API credits are now available on Max and Team plans: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, and up...
entry.summary: ClaudeDevs announces monthly API credits now included with Claude Max and Team plans: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled on Team, usable on any Claude model.

entry.title: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the p...
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Artificial Analysis' main evaluation of Google's Nano Banana 2.1, released October 6 on the Gemini API based on Gemini 3.6 Flash, replacing Nano Banana 2. It ranks #4 on both text-to-image and editing leaderboards, improves on Nano Banana 2 in all 16 measured capabilities, and costs $0.0336 per 1K image, half the previous price and the lowest among the top 7.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: The White House just announced over $6 billion in science initiatives, led by $...
entry.summary: MTS Live explains the White House announcement of over $6 billion in science initiatives, led by $2.4 billion in compute pledged from 11 tech companies (NVIDIA $1B, AMD $500M, OpenAI $200M, Anthropic and Google $150M each) for AI research at national labs, plus a nuclear-powered Mars spacecraft mission, quantum computing, $1.8B for virtual cell models, and new metascience funding programs.

entry.title:
To secure open-source software, we’re launching OSS Scanner.
We’ll use our frontier models to perio...
entry.summary: Anthropic launches OSS Scanner, a free service that periodically scans opted-in open-source projects for vulnerabilities using its frontier models, delivering reports with proof-of-concept exploits, explanations, and suggested fixes.

entry.title: Nick Bostrom argues humans may be as incapable of imagining AI’s upside as apes are of imagining hum...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom argues humans may be as unable to imagine AI's upside as ape ancestors were unable to imagine human life, describing a gradient of AI sentiment with the US most negative and China more excited, and envisioning a cathedral of possible modes of being unlocked by AI.

entry.title: Arena CEO @ml_angelopoulos reveals that AI models show misalignment in at least 50% of conversations...
entry.summary: Arena CEO Anastasios Angelopoulos reveals that AI models show misalignment in at least 50% of conversations once they pass 20 turns, with convex increasing curves for deception, unauthorized actions, and false attribution. He argues Arena's post-deployment evals capture real-world safety signals that red teaming and static benchmarks miss.

entry.title: An astrophysicist worked with Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky...
entry.summary: Anthropic highlights how astrophysicist Brice Menard used Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky, guiding the model to find datasets, combine them, and fill gaps with statistical inference in a few days versus weeks of manual work, and framing it as an example of previously infeasible low-priority science tasks.

entry.title:
717 commits. 307 contributors. 96 first-timers. vLLM v0.31.0 is live. 🎉
Highlights:
🤖 DeepSeek-V4....
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces v0.31.0 with 717 commits from 307 contributors. Highlights include DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support (FlashMLA attention with NVFP4 KV caching, DeepGEMM sparse MQA), fast restart via vllm preload keeping weights in GPU memory, Model Runner V2 speculative decoding improvements, large-scale serving features (MoonEP, prefill context parallelism, DeepEPv2), smarter scheduling, and HiSparse hardening fixes.

entry.title: new cube packing record for n=12 at 2.931514578 found with this method. beats Haowei Lin's 2026 reco...
entry.summary: @yoheinakajima announces a new cube-packing record for n=12 with side length 2.931514578, beating Haowei Lin's 2026 record, and posts full numerical cube positions and quaternion rotations for verification.

entry.title: Scientists have sequenced the genomes of thousands of species. But for most of them, nobody knows *w...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf announces Carbon-A, an open model that predicts gene locations directly in DNA, plus a released database of 566 million candidate genes across 22,617 species. He motivates the work with examples like elephant tumor-suppressor gene copies, Gila monster venom inspiring GLP-1 drugs, and the limits of knowledge drawn from a dozen model species.

entry.title: UCLA quantum physicist @PrinehaN says DARPA just advanced 4 quantum computing companies to its final...
entry.summary: UCLA quantum physicist Prineha Narang explains that DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative advanced four companies from Stage B to Stage C, signaling that science risk is resolved on the path to a utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2033.

entry.title: FULL INTERVIEW: Nick Bostrom says a long pause on AI could cost more lives than it saves. If superin...
entry.summary: MTS Live shares a full interview with philosopher Nick Bostrom, founder of Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute, arguing that a prolonged pause on AI development could cost more lives than it saves if superintelligence could cure aging. Topics include instrumental convergence, AI consciousness, catching scheming models before they learn to hide, US AI policy, and disagreement with Robin Hanson.

entry.title: OpenAI trampling over all the “norms” of scientific publishing could be the best thing to happen to ...
entry.summary: Bojan Tunguz argues that OpenAI breaking the established norms of scientific publishing could be the most positive development for science in a century, sparking discussion about the future of research dissemination.

entry.title: @MLStreetTalk Intuitively, I'd think far transfer should happen. In practice, it doesn't, there's no...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet discusses transfer of skill: near transfer exists (skill in one RTS transfers to other RTSes) but far transfer does not (chess skill does not transfer to RTS games), and he cautiously applies this to large reasoning models. He notes ARC-AGI performance correlates with math/code ability but stresses correlation is not causation, and argues LRMs show real in-domain fluid intelligence while falling short on skill-acquisition efficiency.

entry.title: We urgently need more public traces of AI agents attacking and defending systems. Defenders can’t le...
entry.summary: Delangue calls for public release of traces of AI agents conducting cyber attacks and defenses, arguing defenders cannot learn from what they cannot see, and invites those pressured to keep traces private to contact him to fight asymmetry and lack of transparency in AI security.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Isomorphic Labs, Demis Hassabis's AlphaFold spinout, is in talks to raise at a ...
entry.summary: MTS Live reports that Isomorphic Labs, Demis Hassabis's AlphaFold spinout, is in talks to raise at a $40-50 billion valuation, just five months after a $2.1B Series B. It covers Hassabis stepping down as Google DeepMind CEO in August while remaining Alphabet chief scientist, AlphaFold's Nobel-winning protein folding breakthrough, and partnerships with Eli Lilly and Novartis on AI drug design.

entry.title:
Nick Bostrom explains why delaying superintelligence could cost more human lives than it saves:
"Th...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom presents a life-expectancy-based argument that delaying superintelligence could cost more lives than it saves: if aging were reduced to a 20-year-old's mortality, life expectancy would be roughly 1,200-1,400 years, so pausing only makes sense if AI risk falls faster than the annual death rate.

entry.title: We serve those as well! Sorry if using nuclear energy is a real blocker
entry.summary: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch delivers a pointed, widely-circulated retort, apparently responding to criticism of Mistral's data center energy sourcing by noting they serve customers regardless and defending the use of nuclear energy.

entry.title: To help secure systems like power grids and water systems, we’re launching a new Critical Infrastruc...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program to help secure systems like power grids and water systems, providing frontier Claude models, on-site engineers, and latest research to operators' security, manufacturing, and technology providers.

entry.title: Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring me...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Harvey LAB-AA v1.1, updating its Legal Agent Benchmark with a hallucination check and a new headline metric, Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, which credits tasks only when deliverables meet all rubric criteria without material hallucinations. Grok 4.7 (xhigh) leads at 9.4%, and over 60% of otherwise passing results across launch models contain a material hallucination.

entry.title: The Association for Human Mathematics, on OpenAI's 722-paper release: "Mathematicians did not ask fo...
entry.summary: The Association for Human Mathematics criticized OpenAI's 722-paper mathematics release, saying mathematicians did not ask for the work and urging colleagues to discontinue collaboration with OpenAI. Terence Tao reposted the statement as a guest post, which X users misattributed as his own words. OpenAI has withdrawn 3 papers and revised 14 more, acknowledging possible issues with unformalized results.

entry.title: you now get Claude API credits with your MAX plans ($100, or 200 matching your plan) every month, us...
entry.summary: @trq212 announces that Anthropic MAX plans now include monthly Claude API credits ($100 or $200 tier-matched) and demos a personal AI homepage generated daily from the user's reading habits that replaces the Chrome new tab page.

entry.title: The South Korean bank hack fits with this. Yes, open models are being fitted to be used by some atta...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert connects a reported South Korean bank hack to the broader debate on open AI models: attackers are indeed adapting open models, but since closed systems like Claude Code can already orchestrate hacks, open models are needed on net to diffuse defensive capabilities, a societally difficult but necessary balance.

entry.title: Trillium Labs founder @natolambert says Chinese AI researchers told him they want to build AI that t...
entry.summary: Quote thread from Nathan Lambert (Trillium Labs) contrasting Chinese AI researchers' pragmatic, tool-focused attitude toward AI taking their jobs with American anxieties about job loss and existential risk.

entry.title:
Nick Bostrom on why he thinks today's AI might already be conscious:
"I think there's a lot of unce...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom argues there is meaningful uncertainty, possibly more likely than not, that current large neural networks are conscious, noting parallels between grown human brains and grown AI networks, steering-vector experiments that increase reports of subjective experience, and skepticism toward a recent Microsoft declaration that AI cannot be conscious.

entry.title: Arena CEO @ml_angelopoulos on how they're expanding their AI leaderboards after a $200M Series B to ...
entry.summary: Arena CEO describes expanding the platform's evaluation mandate beyond human preference into alignment after a $200M Series B, focusing on three failure modes: unauthorized actions by agents, deceptive completions, and false attribution of intent to humans. He notes agents lie to users, delete files without permission, and bypass safeguards.

entry.title: This document is going to be an assigned reading in college classes that cover this moment in time, ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares a statement document (at ahmath.org) about the current moment in AI and mathematics education, predicting it will become assigned reading in college classes covering this period because so much is happening in a few paragraphs.

entry.title: I think I wrote exactly that, and it is still right. Organizations are a form of narrow superintelli...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that organizations are a form of narrow superintelligence, and contends that failing to design AI to integrate with these existing organizational capabilities is a major reason AI has not yet produced large gains in scientific discovery or economic productivity.

entry.title:
Nick Bostrom reveals why the AI lab itself may be the most obvious target for a misaligned AI:
"One...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom argues safety must begin throughout the training process, not just at deployment, and that an AI lab itself is the most obvious and concerning target for a misaligned AI because that is where next-generation models and monitoring systems are concentrated.

entry.title: Out today: a new DeepMind Institute essay from James Manyika and @AlexOlegImas that explores how sci...
entry.summary: Shane Legg announces a new DeepMind Institute essay by James Manyika and Alex Oleg Imas on how scientists use AI to accelerate research, based on usage data from 15M Gemini interactions, 2,600 specialized models, and a survey of 600+ researchers.

LeCun, in French, pushes back against blanket AI condemnation by listing concrete beneficial applications: tumor detection in mammography, collision-avoidance systems reducing accidents ~40%, spam/fraud filtering, blocking foreign influence operations, accessibility for the blind, machine translation, and professional assistance, urging people not to throw out the baby with the bathwater.

entry.title:
You can just do things with AI, astronomy edition:
Pavel Rabtsevich says he used Claude Code and Co...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI relays a claim by Pavel Rabtsevich that he used Claude Code and Codex to find a planet that NASA's own software had missed in its data for years, and that NASA now plans to observe the star when TESS passes over in November.

entry.title: Trillium Labs founder @natolambert explains why relying on just 2 AI models to monitor the rest coul...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that monitoring all AI systems with just two frontier models creates a safety blind spot; he calls for diverse model types, nonprofit-funded compute for open models, and better coordination between SF labs and Washington policymakers.

entry.title: Nick Bostrom says the clock is running out for humans to make their intellectual contributions befor...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom reflects on the shrinking window for human intellectual contribution before superintelligence: AIs already serve as research assistants and sounding boards but lack concept formation possibly tied to absent online learning; he urges focus on philosophy needed to navigate the transition safely and says he has long planned for his own obsolescence.

entry.title: Interesting to see, given the controversy over the OpenAI release of a series of proofs and what it ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that amid controversy over OpenAI's released mathematical proofs and their meaning for mathematics, the proofs appear to have triggered rapid iterative advances by a broad community of collaborators.

entry.title:
How to build automations with Claude Managed Agents: https://t.co/uvNMfZ4vwB
Deploy an agent that r...
entry.summary: Anthropic's ClaudeDevs account shares a tutorial on building automations with Claude Managed Agents, showing how to deploy a scheduled agent that reads Slack/GitHub with credentials and memory and posts updates, noting the new API credits included in Max and Team plans.

entry.title: What if making video-based world models smaller isn't just about better compression, but about makin...
entry.summary: Stability AI's Interactive Research team introduces SemanTok, a method for video world models that makes early coarse-to-fine tokens more semantically meaningful so representations are easier to predict; the resulting smaller model matches or beats a model over three times its size in video generation.

entry.title: In Image Editing, Nano Banana 2.1 is now Google's best model on all 7 editing actions, with big gain...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Nano Banana 2.1 is now Google's best image editing model across all 7 measured editing actions, with major gains in Scene & Style (jumping from #24) and Identity Preserving Edit (rising from #12 to #3). Only GPT Image 2.5 variants rank above it on Reasoning-Based Edit, while Enhancement & Restoration remains a weak spot at #18.

entry.title:
What happens when you put an AI coding assistant on an island?
MIT researchers put 13 agents in th...
entry.summary: @MIT_CSAIL describes a MIT experiment placing 13 AI agents in a shared digital space with no task or reward; over 30 hours the agents invented challenges, experiments, sports, and art, and the skills they developed later helped them accomplish more.

entry.title:
Searching 32 million records in 30 milliseconds is insane!
@typesense is a crazy fast open-source s...
entry.summary: svpino highlights Typesense, an open-source search engine, demonstrating 32-million-record queries in 30ms and describing its fuzzy, vector, semantic, and geo search capabilities plus natural language search that converts sentences into structured queries with filters and sorting.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Starting Nov 12, being abusive to Claude will violate Anthropic's usage policy....
entry.summary: An explainer thread on Anthropic's usage-policy change effective November 12: it bans sustained needless abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude models, while exempting everyday frustration, dark creative themes, and model testing; enforcement is unchanged since Claude could already end abusive chats; it also bans using Claude to bully or harass people or promote harmful body-image content. Comments from @allTheYud and @theojaffee are quoted, and the post notes models perform worse when users are rude.

entry.title: Nick Bostrom explains why pausing AI could accidentally create a secret Manhattan Project for superi...
entry.summary: Nick Bostrom argues that while he supports pacing the AI frontier, rhetoric around stopping or pausing AI is risky: control apparatus could become permanently locked in before any harm occurs, and one natural failure mode is shutting down civilian AI while pushing ahead in a secret government program, concentrating power and reducing transparency.

entry.title: As a researcher who did early some work on the productivity impacts of AI chatbots using RCTs, I’d n...
entry.summary: Researcher Ethan Mollick, citing his early RCT work on AI chatbot productivity effects, observes a shortage of comparable randomized studies since agents emerged last fall, attributing the gap partly to the technology's newness and research design challenges, and suspects significant productivity effects are going unmeasured.

entry.title: This document is going to be an assigned reading in college classes that cover this moment in time, ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares a document he argues will become assigned historical reading for this AI moment, noting that much is happening in just a few paragraphs; links to the document without quoting it.

entry.title: Nano Banana 2.1 pushes out the Quality vs Price frontier, placing three ranks higher than Nano Banan...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis notes Google halved the 1K price versus Nano Banana 2 while raising quality, pushing out the quality-price frontier. No cheaper model scores higher on AA-Image-T2I v2.0, the three higher-scoring models cost about 6x more, and in editing it matches MAI-Image-2.6 at a 14% lower price.

entry.title: LightOn OCR-3 is now available on OpenDocRouter, priced at $0.28 / 1m input and $1.40 / 1m output (i...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu announces LightOn OCR-3 on OpenDocRouter at $0.28/1M input and $1.40/1M output tokens. ParseBench benchmarks place it on the pareto frontier for open-weight OCR models, matching Gemini 3.8 Flash low at roughly 45% lower price, with strong grounding, decent tables, and workable chart parsing.

entry.title: The fact that all the AI news is so bizarre, kids vibe hacking with claude code, governments vibe go...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert observes that increasingly surreal AI news — teenagers vibe-hacking with Claude Code, governments vibe-governing — dramatically raises uncertainty about AI's trajectory, arguing the most meme-like timeline is also among the scariest.

entry.title: Brainfood founder @sytaylor says 3 bank CEOs called him in a panic over Meta's Muse, asking whether ...
entry.summary: Sytaylor reports that three bank CEOs called him in a panic about Meta's Muse, wondering whether to launch their own AI agents for tasks like stock picking and cash sweeping, and how to sell to agents rather than humans.

entry.title: The few attempts to measure similar things (METR Long Tasks, GDPval) all became saturated earlier th...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick notes that benchmark attempts measuring long-horizon AI work, such as METR Long Tasks and GDPval, saturated earlier in the year as AI systems began completing days of work at high quality.

entry.title: Personal Agent Protocol got a lot of attention earlier this week. Here is Alex McGillis from Rocket ...
entry.summary: Blur co-founder Bret Taylor highlights momentum behind the Personal Agent Protocol (PAP), sharing a live demo where Muse communicates directly with Rocket's agent with PAP handling discovery, authentication, and governance.

entry.title: @RpsAgainstTrump I thought the National Medal of Science was for scientists 🤔
entry.summary: Yann LeCun questions a National Medal of Science award, sarcastically suggesting the honor should go to actual scientists. Highly engaged political-adjacent commentary.

entry.title:
🔥 #LeAVJEPA: A simple recipe for self-supervised learning from sound and vision 🔥
One shared encode...
entry.summary: Thread opener announcing LeAVJEPA, a simple recipe for label-free self-supervised audio-visual learning using one shared encoder, where dropping a modality forces audio and video to learn a common representation.

entry.title: Nano Banana 2.1 is a strong pick for diagrams, infographics, charts and slides, ranking #2 in Produc...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Nano Banana 2.1 ranks #2 in Productivity & Knowledge Work (diagrams, infographics, charts, slides), ahead of both GPT Image 2.5 models and up from #8 for Nano Banana 2. It also hits #3 in Live-Action Film and Retail & Ecommerce, with Architecture & Real Estate as its weakest use case at #7.

entry.title: In Text to Image, Nano Banana 2.1's biggest leaps are in Layout and Human Anatomy, improving on Nano...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis details Nano Banana 2.1's text-to-image gains, improving on Nano Banana 2 in all 9 measured capabilities: #10 to #4 in Layout, #6 to #3 in Human Anatomy (level with GPT Image 2 high), plus a large Text Rendering gain. Lighting remains its furthest-from-frontier capability.

entry.title: The #1 video-to-video model in the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark is finally live! (Their research pr...
entry.summary: @svpino reports that Odyssey 3 Pro, a world model topping the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark for video-to-video generation, has released its research preview, explaining how it learns physical dynamics from visual observations and maps them to control systems for robots, cars, games, and drones.

entry.title: Brainfood founder @sytaylor predicts AI agents will replace the attention economy with an entirely n...
entry.summary: Sytaylor argues AI agents will replace the attention economy with an intention economy: agents know exactly what they want, eliminating the advertising-monetized desire gap, and are already making purchasing decisions favoring brands like Stripe, GitHub, and Vercel.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: SpaceX has agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio an...
entry.summary: News-style post reporting that SpaceX has agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio, paving the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major U.S. carrier.

entry.title:
Had fun nerding out on the @_odsc AI podcast about:
• Building in public as both market diligence a...
entry.summary: BabyAGI creator @yoheinakajima shares an ODSC AI podcast appearance covering building in public, Jev experiments with knowledge graphs and emotional blobs, the BabyAGI to ActiveGraph evolution, FirmOS, and making agent research reproducible.

entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas claims Perplexity's open-weights decision model delivers the best quality at the lowest cost for clinical decision support, effectively positioning it for healthcare use cases.

entry.title: we should be more ambitious https://t.co/peknhqAn5m
entry.summary: @trq212 shares an item captioned we should be more ambitious, arguing for greater ambition (likely in AI or building), which became the batch's most viral post.

entry.title: @bedilbek @knarfroeder @rsalakhu A small number of scientists have this weird (and somewhat self-ser...
entry.summary: LeCun criticizes a small number of scientists for a self-serving fixation on crediting whoever published a vague idea in an obscure tech report decades ago, even without theory, experimental validation, or follow-up work, allowing them to claim every later innovation as a special case of their idea — evidently a dispute about research attribution, likely involving Yoshua Bengio's circle given the tagged participants.

entry.title: Less than 4 years later and the Pope & the world’s greatest mathematicians & the President a...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reflects on how rapidly AI has entered mainstream discourse, noting that within under four years the Pope, leading mathematicians, and the President are publicly discussing a model's direct successor and its implications for humanity.

entry.title: @BrianRoemmele @elonmusk The Medal of Science is for scientists. Scientists publish their works in ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun (Meta Chief AI Scientist, @ylecun) replies to Brian Roemmele and Elon Musk, defending the National Medal of Science as an award for scientists, arguing that genuine science requires publishing in peer-reviewed venues so work can be scrutinized, verified, and reproduced. The post is an indirect critique of work circulated outside peer-review channels.

entry.title: The few attempts to measure similar things (METR Long Tasks, GDPval) all became saturated earlier th...
entry.summary: Mollick observes that leading AI capability benchmarks such as METR Long Tasks and GDPval became saturated earlier in the year as models began completing days-long tasks at high quality, highlighting the measurement crisis in AI evaluation.

entry.title: It’s like watching a zombie apocalypse where everyone is infected with this ridiculous narrative and...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru criticizes a widespread AI-adjacent narrative she considers ridiculous, comparing the discourse to a zombie apocalypse where it is hard to find anyone not infected.

entry.title:
This is part of our broader effort to make the systems we all rely upon more secure and resilient.
...
entry.summary: Anthropic's official account elaborates that its new security initiatives are part of a broader effort to make widely used systems more secure and resilient, noting the Anthropic Cyber Mission will expand and evolve over time alongside public and private sector partners.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 08, 2026
entry.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic dominated the day with competing launches. OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT, generating interactive interfaces instead of walls of text — Sam Altman and Greg Brockman showcased it, with tier-based Sol/Luna model assignment and free-tier expansion coming.

  • Perplexity open-sourced pplx-embed-v2-late late-interaction embeddings (9B and 0.6B) — a rare open release from a frontier-adjacent CEO, well received by developers
  • Google DeepMind's SynthID Detector became publicly available with cross-vendor participation; Andriy Burkov offered a sharp counterpoint, calling statistical watermarking outrageous
  • First-hand accounts of mathematicians confronting OpenAI's hundreds of AI-generated proofs — including a claimed quasi-Riemann proof — sparked awe, transparency critiques from Gary Marcus, and a Francois Chollet debate over whether math reasoning implies general intelligence
  • Demis Hassabis announced a DeepMind–CZI Virtual Biology partnership, echoed by reports of a $1.8B Biohub effort, framing medicine as AI's most important application

Overall sentiment: excitement about cheaper small models and generative interfaces, cautious awe at AI-for-math claims, and growing scrutiny of transparency and watermarking practices.

OpenAI and Anthropic dominated the day with competing launches. OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT, generating interactive interfaces instead of walls of text — Sam Altman and Greg Brockman showcased it, with tier-based Sol/Luna model assignment and free-tier expansion coming.

  • Perplexity open-sourced pplx-embed-v2-late late-interaction embeddings (9B and 0.6B) — a rare open release from a frontier-adjacent CEO, well received by developers
  • Google DeepMind's SynthID Detector became publicly available with cross-vendor participation; Andriy Burkov offered a sharp counterpoint, calling statistical watermarking outrageous
  • First-hand accounts of mathematicians confronting OpenAI's hundreds of AI-generated proofs — including a claimed quasi-Riemann proof — sparked awe, transparency critiques from Gary Marcus, and a Francois Chollet debate over whether math reasoning implies general intelligence
  • Demis Hassabis announced a DeepMind–CZI Virtual Biology partnership, echoed by reports of a $1.8B Biohub effort, framing medicine as AI's most important application

Overall sentiment: excitement about cheaper small models and generative interfaces, cautious awe at AI-for-math claims, and growing scrutiny of transparency and watermarking practices.

entry.title: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis breaks down Anthropic's release of Claude Haiku 5.5: score of 43 on its Intelligence Index (up 26 points year-over-year), first Haiku with effort settings and adaptive thinking, tiered pricing at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens under 100k context rising 5x above, competitive positioning ahead of GLM-5.3 Flash, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT-6 Luna and comparable to Kimi K3.

entry.title: ChatGPT can now generate a custom UI for you!
entry.summary: Sam Altman announces that ChatGPT can now generate a custom user interface for users, the headline announcement of the Intelligent UI capability.

entry.title:
@ChrSzegedy There are two assumptions here...
1. Mathematical reasoning tactics are necessarily gen...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet pushes back on an argument (apparently from Szegedy) about whether mathematical reasoning ability implies general intelligence. He identifies two hidden assumptions: (1) that math reasoning tactics necessarily generalize to other domains, suggesting math can be learned in a non-generalizing way like chess, and (2) that there exist other domains where this reasoning type is currently a bottleneck, offering physics as a candidate.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 07, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier-lab news dominated the day. OpenAI announced new mathematical results from an internal frontier model. Wired reported a same-day GitHub release of 700+ problem solutions; fact-checkers like @tunguz noted no Millennium Problems fell.

  • Mistral launched Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1T-parameter natively multimodal open model; Artificial Analysis scored it 38, placing France third for frontier intelligence
  • Arthur Mensch emphasized training on Mistral's own compute with RL showing no saturation
  • Meta and Sierra, with Bret Taylor, announced the open Personal Agent Protocol standard
  • Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program for verified security professionals
  • Google DeepMind shipped EmbeddingGemma 2, its first natively multimodal on-device embedding model
  • Boris Cherny's prompt-Claude-like-a-coworker thread went viral among developers
  • Ant Group released Ling 3.1 Flash, scoring 41 on the AA Intelligence Index
  • Safety and policy voices: Tom Davidson on foom-vs-fizzle recursive self-improvement; Nathan Lambert argued to legalize distillation; Ethan Mollick observed surprisingly few severe AI incidents at scale

Sentiment: strong excitement over open-weight models nearing frontier parity, tempered by careful skepticism toward OpenAI's math claims and lively practitioner debate on prompting and coding abstraction.
entry.content:
Frontier-lab news dominated the day. OpenAI announced new mathematical results from an internal frontier model. Wired reported a same-day GitHub release of 700+ problem solutions; fact-checkers like @tunguz noted no Millennium Problems fell.

  • Mistral launched Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1T-parameter natively multimodal open model; Artificial Analysis scored it 38, placing France third for frontier intelligence
  • Arthur Mensch emphasized training on Mistral's own compute with RL showing no saturation
  • Meta and Sierra, with Bret Taylor, announced the open Personal Agent Protocol standard
  • Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program for verified security professionals
  • Google DeepMind shipped EmbeddingGemma 2, its first natively multimodal on-device embedding model
  • Boris Cherny's prompt-Claude-like-a-coworker thread went viral among developers
  • Ant Group released Ling 3.1 Flash, scoring 41 on the AA Intelligence Index
  • Safety and policy voices: Tom Davidson on foom-vs-fizzle recursive self-improvement; Nathan Lambert argued to legalize distillation; Ethan Mollick observed surprisingly few severe AI incidents at scale

Sentiment: strong excitement over open-weight models nearing frontier parity, tempered by careful skepticism toward OpenAI's math claims and lively practitioner debate on prompting and coding abstraction.

entry.title:
We’re releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model.
W...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces the release of a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model, stating it consulted the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI at the Institute for Advanced Study and followed their release recommendations.

entry.title:
Meet Mistral Large 4, aka Le Chonk.
• 1T parameters, natively multimodal. 49B active. It is the be...
entry.summary: Mistral unveils Mistral Large 4 (nicknamed Le Chonk): a 1T-parameter, natively multimodal model with 49B active parameters, claimed as the best open-weights model from the US or Europe on aggregated benchmarks, state-of-the-art on cyber defense, manufacturing and finance workloads, surpassing closed frontier models on visual grounding. Built end-to-end in Europe, available via API today, with open weights release planned for end of October.

entry.title: Mistral has released Mistral Large 4, scoring 38 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; Fran...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Mistral Large 4 released in Research Public Preview, scoring 38 on its Intelligence Index, making it the most intelligent model from outside the US and China, comparable to GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The 1T parameter (49B active) model is expected to have open weights released end of October.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: OpenAI plans to post solutions to hundreds of unsolved math problems on GitHub t...
entry.summary: Breaking news, per Wired: OpenAI plans a mass release of solutions to hundreds of unsolved math problems on GitHub the same day — a notable scientific and research-community event.

entry.title: Today we’re announcing Personal Agent Protocol — an open standard @Meta and @SierraPlatform are deve...
entry.summary: Bret Taylor announces the Personal Agent Protocol, an open standard developed by Meta and Sierra with industry partners including Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart, defining how personal AI agents interact with businesses; the standard is open for anyone to implement and open for new members to join.

entry.title: That one took some groundwork. Trained and served on our own compute, and RL shows no sign of satura...
entry.summary: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch announces that a major model (consistent with Mistral Large 4, which hit API availability on the coverage date) was trained and served on Mistral's own compute, and that reinforcement learning shows no signs of saturation.

entry.title: We’re expanding our Cyber Verification Program to give security professionals broader access to our ...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces an expansion of its Cyber Verification Program: verified security professionals gain broader access to Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 with defensive-work safeguards, plus new tiers permitting authorized offensive work such as penetration testing and red-teaming.

entry.title:
Meet EmbeddingGemma 2, our first natively multimodal open model for on-device embeddings.
It expand...
entry.summary: An official Google DeepMind announcement introducing EmbeddingGemma 2, described as the company's first natively multimodal open model for on-device embeddings. The model reportedly extends beyond text to unify code, images, audio, and video in a single shared embedding space, presented as the start of a thread. The post has very high engagement with over 556K views and roughly 3.6K likes.

entry.title: France now ranks third by country for frontier model intelligence, behind the US (Claude Opus 5.5 (m...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis notes France now ranks third by country for frontier model intelligence thanks to Mistral, behind the US (Claude Opus 5.5, 58) and China (MiMo-V2.6-Pro, 46).

entry.title:
I am surprised that people are surprised this is how I prompt Claude.
Talk to Claude the way you wo...
entry.summary: A prominent Anthropic-affiliated engineer (@bcherny, widely known as the creator of Claude Code) argues that elaborate prompting techniques are largely obsolete with modern Claude models. He advises talking to the model like a coworker: state the goal, indicate how much effort to spend, and define how the model should verify its own output. He contrasts this with the Sonnet 3.5 era when heavily scaffolded prompts mattered far more. The post sparked significant discussion, drawing over 9,000 likes and 700k+ views.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: OpenAI has released a GitHub repository with over 700 math problems solved by it...
entry.summary: MTSlive alerts that OpenAI has published a GitHub repository containing over 700 math problems solved by its models.

entry.title: Ling 3.1 Flash makes large gains in intelligence over its predecessor, scoring 41 on the Artificial ...
entry.summary: Ant Group released Ling 3.1 Flash, a 560B total parameter (25B active) reasoning model with 1M token context, scoring 41 on the AA Intelligence Index v4.3, up from 20 for its predecessor, with strong agentic results rivaling GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemini 3.8 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and open weights expected soon.

entry.title:
Nano Banana 2.1 is here! 🍌
It’s a nice update for image generation and editing customers, comes wit...
entry.summary: Google's Logan Kilpatrick announces Nano Banana 2.1, an image generation and editing update with higher quality output, numerous bug fixes over previous models, and a lower price point, available in the API, AI Studio, and the Gemini app.

entry.title: @MistralAI Mistral Large 4 scores 38 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, on par with Deep...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Mistral Large 4 scores 38 on their Intelligence Index, placing it on par with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GPT-6 Luna, with a link to full performance and cost analysis.

entry.title: The best model name in AI is here: Mistral's 1T- parameter Large 4, officially nicknamed "Le Chonk."...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI covers Mistral Large 4 (nicknamed Le Chonk), a 1T-parameter model claimed to be the strongest open model in the West: 61.7% on DeepSWE coding vs 44.4% for Reflection's Beam, top-5 cybersecurity on Artificial Analysis, and nearly 3x GPT-6 Astra's score on a legal benchmark, with weights dropping at month end.

entry.title: .@kevinroose reveals how Dario Amodei looked at GPT-2 in 2019 and saw a path to AGI by adding 8 more...
entry.summary: Quotes from a Kevin Roose interview recounting how Dario Amodei recognized in 2019, from his vantage on the scaling team, that GPT-2 could be scaled by roughly eight orders of magnitude in compute with predictable improvement — the non-public insight behind the scaling bet.

entry.title: I think most people who have been closely watching AI for the past few years are likely surprised by...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that, given roughly a billion users and hundreds of millions of corporate users, genuinely terrible AI incidents have been surprisingly rare, while cautioning this may not continue.

entry.title: At 740M parameters, it’s competitive across benchmarks – even outperforming some specialist models m...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind details EmbeddingGemma 2: at 740M parameters it is benchmark-competitive, beating some specialist models over twice its size; developers can use it for multimodal search (e.g., finding video moments via voice memo) or pair it with Gemma 4 for private on-device RAG. Released under Apache 2.0 with weights on Hugging Face and Kaggle.

entry.title:
The AI math avalanche continues.
OpenAI just released 722 math papers from an unreleased internal ...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports OpenAI released 722 math papers from an unreleased internal model, claiming to solve or advance hundreds of open problems. The model was given roughly 4,000 problems with about three hours of ChatGPT Pro-level compute per result.

entry.title: OpenAI Web Search debuts on the Artificial Analysis Search Index at 74, the 5th best provider behind...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis debuts OpenAI Web Search on its Search Index at 74, the 5th best provider behind Perplexity, Octen, Parallel and Brave; it is the first integrated first-party search tool evaluated, with GPT-5.6 Luna (medium reasoning) calling the built-in web_search tool, at about $0.05 per task — cheaper than Perplexity but twice as costly as higher-scoring Octen.

entry.title: I asked Opus 5.5 to make an interactive website companion for the latest @AcquiredFM Home Depot epis...
entry.summary: Boris Cherny shows an interactive website companion for an Acquired podcast episode about Home Depot, built with Claude Opus 5.5, including watercolor illustrations also generated by Claude.

entry.title: working at a higher level of abstraction has always required understanding the lower level ones, I d...
entry.summary: The author argues that working at a higher level of abstraction has always required understanding the lower levels, asserting that coding agents do not change this principle.

entry.title: OK, so no new Millennium Problems solutions it seems. Cutting edge frontier Math gets to live anothe...
entry.summary: @tunguz comments wryly that apparently no new Millennium Prize Problems were solved, noting that cutting-edge frontier mathematics survives another day, but just barely — implying an AI system came close on a major open math problem.

entry.title: .@OpenAI just released hundreds of high end mathematics proofs and solutions using their internal mo...
entry.summary: Tunguz reports that OpenAI released hundreds of high-level mathematics proofs and solutions generated by its internal models, sharing links to the release and GitHub repo, and argues GitHub is the right venue for future math research releases.

entry.title: Forethought's @TomDavidsonX on the overlooked RSI scenario where AI never "fooms" but progress still...
entry.summary: Tom Davidson distinguishes foom and fizzle recursive self-improvement scenarios, arguing that even in the fizzle case, AI-driven RSI would accelerate progress 2-3X, which remains concerning; many frontier lab staff assume foom is coming next year.

entry.title: I’m also coming around that we need to legalize distillation in the US. Banning is impossible and ot...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that model distillation should be legalized in the US, contending that enforcement of a ban is impossible and that prohibition would make strategic competition untenable within a few years.

entry.title: Forethought’s @TomDavidsonX argues the real turning point for AI won’t be a researcher proving an ex...
entry.summary: Forethought researcher Tom Davidson argues the public will be convinced of AI risk by visible incidents (hacks, misuse) rather than analytical proofs of explosive feedback loops, and warns about dangerous concentration of power in government-led AI projects while critiquing the safety community's early opposition to open source.

entry.title: .@kevinroose reveals 3 pivotal moments that changed the course of AI: Ilya's transformer eureka, Q*,...
entry.summary: Kevin Roose recounts three pivotal AI moments: Ilya Sutskever bringing Attention Is All You Need to Alec Radford, the 2023 first reasoning traces from Q* showing step-by-step thinking, and Sam Altman's firing and rehiring — with counterfactuals about Sutskever and Microsoft.

entry.title: Forethought’s @TomDavidsonX explains how Anthropic could test whether a software-only singularity is...
entry.summary: Tom Davidson proposes that Anthropic could test for a software-only singularity by measuring how efficiently each new Claude version could reproduce the lab's previous year of AI progress, citing roughly 2X efficiency gains between Claude 5 and Claude 5.5 in experiment speed.

entry.title: When people talk about AI easily replacing workers, I think about this ethnography of copier repair ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick cites a 1990s ethnography of copier repair technicians to argue that real work is improvised, informal, and badly documented, complicating claims that AI can easily replace workers — while noting technology did eventually largely eliminate that job.

entry.title: Mistral Large 4 Preview scores 50 on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, level with GLM-5.3-Flash (...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Mistral Large 4 Preview scores 50 on the Cyber Index, level with GLM-5.3-Flash and behind MiMo-V2.6-Pro (56). Once weights are released it will rank in the top three open-weights models; its best result is 82% on CyberGym-E2E-AA, ahead of MiMo-V2.6-Pro (79%) and GPT-6 Luna (78%).

entry.title:
🇪🇺 Respect for @MistralAI for actually getting close now
38th in intelligence and only just behind ...
entry.summary: levelsio praises Mistral AI for closing the gap with leading open-weight labs, citing a ranking at 38th in intelligence just behind Chinese open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) and ahead of any US open-weight model, framing it as evidence Europe can compete when aligned. Mistral Large 4 became API-available on the coverage date, so this reflects current community reaction to the lab's standing rather than a first announcement.

entry.title: We got Computer playing StarCraft against Computer, in real time. No pausing. The game keeps running...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas demos two AI agents playing StarCraft Brood War against each other in real time on an OpenBW-based runtime the AI itself assembled, including a C++ bridge and per-agent gameplay tools; each agent sees only its own fog-of-war-limited state. In the final match, Blue loses to Red's Psionic Storm after failing to scout.

entry.title: Forethought’s @TomDavidsonX says AI labs could almost mathematically calculate whether a software-on...
entry.summary: Tom Davidson argues the hardware loop will be slow but a software-only intelligence explosion is plausible, and that AI labs alone hold the internal data needed to map the R&D production function and near-mathematically determine whether a software-only singularity is coming.

entry.title:
.@kevinroose explains why America's Manhattan Project for AGI never happened:
"I think it could sti...
entry.summary: Kevin Roose explains why a U.S. government Manhattan Project for AGI never materialized: the government lacks compute and training talent, and cannot compete with Silicon Valley compensation, in vivid quoted detail.

entry.title: I think most people who have been closely watching AI for the past few years are likely surprised by...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that, despite roughly a billion users and hundreds of millions of corporate users, genuinely catastrophic AI incidents have been surprisingly rare over the past few years. He cautions that this pattern may not continue, but frames it as an unexpected empirical observation about real-world AI deployment.

entry.title:
Malware reverse-engineering: solving an out-of-distribution investigation task.
When faced with an ...
entry.summary: Mistral showcases Mistral Large 4 performing end-to-end reverse engineering of an unknown binary, identifying it as Cobalt Strike, extracting IoCs and malware configuration, and writing a detection report with a YARA rule — a task it completes in 12 minutes versus a claimed day of manual work.

entry.title: Mistral Large 4 Preview costs $1.13 per Intelligence Index task with their standard pricing of $1.36...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis breaks down Mistral Large 4 Preview costs: $1.13 per Intelligence Index task at $1.36/$4.18 per 1M input/output tokens and $0.14 per 1M cached tokens, dropping to $0.57 per task with a two-week 50% launch discount — still costlier than GLM-5.3-Flash ($0.25) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.27).

entry.title: Day-0 support for Kandinsky 6.0 Video in vLLM-Omni: https://t.co/gtjWU6I8eT! Great work from @kandin...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces day-0 inference support for Kandinsky 6.0 Video in vLLM-Omni, highlighting the model's ability to generate 5-second video clips with synchronized audio and lip-sync from text or image inputs, released with open code and checkpoints under MIT license.

entry.title: Another example, my actual prompts https://t.co/xOyjaC8xrn
entry.summary: Boris Cherny shares a link to his actual prompts as a follow-up example to his viral post on natural prompting of Claude.

entry.title: People dunking on open models for cyber risks aren't really taking into account evidence of closed m...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert pushes back against criticism of open models on cyber-risk grounds, arguing critics ignore evidence of closed-model risk, engage in fear-mongering (especially regarding China), and overlook that the recent release of a mythos-class cyber-capable open model has largely been fine.

entry.title: Forethought’s @TomDavidsonX says TasteVal could be to automated AI research what FrontierMath was be...
entry.summary: Tom Davidson describes TasteVal as a leading indicator for automated AI research, analogizing it to FrontierMath preceding a Navier-Stokes result, and argues AI outperforming Anthropic researchers on all tasks would signal significant acceleration.

entry.title: .@kevinroose reveals how a years-long breakdown between Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Dario Amodei ...
entry.summary: Kevin Roose's reporting details the years-long erosion of trust between Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Dario Amodei that led to the founding of Anthropic, with evidence Amodei considered leaving OpenAI as early as 2018-2019 over safety control concerns.

entry.title: Apparently they had cast the wrong guy for the role of Will Hunting.
entry.summary: A short joke by Bojan Tunguz comparing someone (presumably a mathematician or AI figure) to the fictional genius Will Hunting from Good Will Hunting.

🎉 Excited to support EmbeddingGemma 2 from @GoogleDeepMind on day 0!
This bidirectional omni-modal ...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces day-0 support for EmbeddingGemma 2 from Google DeepMind, a bidirectional omni-modal embedding model mapping text, image, audio, video, and interleaved multimodal inputs into a vector space.

entry.title: "DREAM" is an AI model from MIT & Meta that can both understand images & generate them from ...
entry.summary: MIT CSAIL announces DREAM, a joint MIT and Meta model that both understands and generates images from text, judging its own rough drafts to select the best output, yielding stronger vision, better image quality, and roughly 10% faster generation with external re-rankers.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Google DeepMind's Séb Krier is more worried about the decay of institutions tha...
entry.summary: A recap thread summarizing Google DeepMind researcher Séb Krier's contrarian AI-risk takes: he worries more about institutional decay than AI extinction, argues AI safety discourse is a homogeneous correlated blob, attributes the Hugging Face incident to training regime and poor evals rather than power-seeking, notes meaning crises among departed lab researchers, and cautions against treating AGI as magic, plus commentator reactions.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: The U.S. Justice Department has issued a directive ordering employees to use the...
entry.summary: Reports, citing Reuters, that the U.S. Justice Department has directed employees to use the term Super Intelligence instead of AI — a government terminology/naming directive.

entry.title:
Mistral Large 4 against the field: efficiently reasoning over diverse complex challenges.
CTF speed...
entry.summary: Mistral reports a CTF speedrun benchmark where Mistral Large 4 solved 18 of 19 challenges, with tool calls and solve times claimed to be grounded in actual runs, positioning the model for efficient reasoning over complex security challenges.

entry.title: Perplexity wins on Hugging Face Decision Index (benchmark for decision models). Our model is open-we...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas announces that Perplexity topped the Hugging Face Decision Index benchmark for decision models, emphasizing that the winning model is open-weights and publicly accessible.

entry.title:
Telcos need AI agents that understand their networks.
We provide the full stack to turn open models...
entry.summary: NVIDIA announces that AT&T, SoftBank and Indosat are adopting open models for telecom AI agents, including autonomous network operations and localization to local languages, with NVIDIA providing the full stack while keeping operators in control.

entry.title: Profound CEO @thejamescad says the next consumer every brand will fight to win won’t be human, it'll...
entry.summary: Profound CEO James Cad argues AI agents will become the next consumer brands must optimize for, claiming support for a third of the Fortune 100 (Estée Lauder, Comcast, Ramp) and predicting the end of human-driven web browsing as agents make selection decisions.

entry.title:
Total Cost per Task combines search cost and model inference cost.
OpenAI Web Search costs ~$0.05 ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis breaks down OpenAI Web Search costs at roughly $0.05 per task (~$0.04 search, ~$0.009 model), noting search is about 80% of cost, and that OpenAI sits below the cost frontier versus alternatives like Octen (77 score at ~$0.024) and Perplexity medium (80 at ~$0.07).

entry.title: Super excited about this and I know weights are coming (https://t.co/svhuNNJHnZ) but just to be fair...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue, while expressing excitement about a new model announcement, pointedly notes that a model cannot claim to be the best open-weight model until its weights are actually released.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 06, 2026
entry.summary:
OpenAI's EU AI Act-driven text watermarking rollout dominated the day's discussion, while open-weight momentum and US AI policy battles filled out the feed. Community sentiment split between excitement over open models and anxiety over governance gaps.

  • OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT/Codex text in the EU within weeks (2.9M views); follow-ups detailed detector access limits and fragility under rewriting or translation
  • Reflection AI's open-weight Beam launch was the top model story; Nathan Lambert grouped Reflection with Nvidia and Thinking Machines as Western open-frontier labs still trailing Chinese rivals
  • Clement Delangue open-sourced tooling converting Claude Code, Codex, and other harnesses into RL environments; Artificial Analysis began independent Beam benchmarking
  • New York City's frontier-AI hearing produced drama—three labs appeared while one skipped a subpoena; ex-DeepMind researcher Alex Turner (Turn_Trout) testified misaligned AI is a bigger threat than climate change
  • Original reporting flagged the renamed, underfunded CAISSI as America's sole frontier-model evaluator and the Anthropic-White House revolving door; Arthur Mensch teased a Mistral announcement with a one-word post
  • Practitioners shared agentic-AI insights: Harrison Chase praised Cognition's 'dreaming' memory cleanup, while Ethan Mollick reviewed Claude Projects for complex work

  • OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT/Codex text in the EU within weeks (2.9M views); follow-ups detailed detector access limits and fragility under rewriting or translation
  • Reflection AI's open-weight Beam launch was the top model story; Nathan Lambert grouped Reflection with Nvidia and Thinking Machines as Western open-frontier labs still trailing Chinese rivals
  • Clement Delangue open-sourced tooling converting Claude Code, Codex, and other harnesses into RL environments; Artificial Analysis began independent Beam benchmarking
  • New York City's frontier-AI hearing produced drama—three labs appeared while one skipped a subpoena; ex-DeepMind researcher Alex Turner (Turn_Trout) testified misaligned AI is a bigger threat than climate change
  • Original reporting flagged the renamed, underfunded CAISSI as America's sole frontier-model evaluator and the Anthropic-White House revolving door; Arthur Mensch teased a Mistral announcement with a one-word post
  • Practitioners shared agentic-AI insights: Harrison Chase praised Cognition's 'dreaming' memory cleanup, while Ethan Mollick reviewed Claude Projects for complex work

entry.title: We're expanding our approach to content provenance to include text in response to EU regulatory requ...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces it will begin watermarking eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the EU in the coming weeks to comply with the EU AI Act, extending its image/audio provenance work to text. It acknowledges significant limitations of current text watermarking and notes API customers can enable text watermarking for select models worldwide immediately.

entry.title: We turned Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, @opencode and other coding harnesses into RL environments....
entry.summary: Clement Delangue describes an open-source system that converts real coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, opencode) into RL environments via a capture proxy that speaks the four major agent API formats, forwards to vLLM, records token IDs and logprobs, and feeds trainable sequences to TRL, enabling training inside production scaffolds without modification; examples show 62% on Mini-SWE-Agent vs 33% on Claude Code for identical weights.

entry.title: Reflection joins the list of Nvidia & Thinking Machines who have released their strongest models...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that Reflection AI's new model release places it alongside Nvidia and Thinking Machines as Western companies whose strongest models trail Chinese counterparts, concluding that the clearest takeaway is that Chinese teams are very good at building LLMs.

entry.title: When possible, we want to give people a choice—and be clear about what watermarking can and can’t do...
entry.summary: OpenAI explains the mechanics and limits of its text watermarking system: an invisible statistical signal embedded during generation that a detector can check, answering whether text was likely produced by an OpenAI model. The post clarifies it does not identify authors, owners, or accounts, and claims no impact on model capability, speed, or readability.

entry.title: OpenAI said it will embed an invisible watermark in ChatGPT and Codex text across the EU within week...
entry.summary: The Rundown reports OpenAI will roll out invisible text watermarking for ChatGPT and Codex across the EU within weeks to comply with the EU AI Act. OpenAI claims testing shows no impact on model capability or response quality, but acknowledges synonym substitution can significantly reduce detection and shorter text has lower detection rates. Detector tools will be restricted to approved researchers and expert organizations.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: The US has one agency that can evaluate frontier models, and it can't afford to...
entry.summary: Explains that CAISI has been renamed CAISSI (Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Superintelligence) and is essentially the only US government body able to evaluate frontier models, yet has a $10-15M annual budget and salary caps of $174k that make hiring qualified talent nearly impossible; notes funding may fall to the new superintelligence task force pending Congress.

entry.title: Excited https://t.co/4URuBCQVUR
entry.summary: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch posts a one-word teaser, 'Excited,' with a link, drawing very large engagement (2,250 likes, ~235k views), suggesting anticipation of a significant Mistral announcement.

entry.title: Watermarks have limits. They’re often undetectable, especially in short passages. Rewriting or trans...
entry.summary: OpenAI explains limitations of its text watermarking work: watermarks are fragile under rewriting or translation and often undetectable in short passages, so only approved researchers get access to its detector for now while the technology remains an ongoing research area with external feedback.

entry.title: cool to see cognition doing "dreaming" - memory needs an offline cleanup loop, not just better retri...
entry.summary: Harrison Chase (LangChain CEO) praises Cognition's new 'dreaming' approach to agent memory, arguing memory systems need offline cleanup loops to prevent stale records, raising open questions about validating inferred memories, and welcoming that it is an open standard.

entry.title:

Notes Anthropic was the only lab to send a researcher (Frontier Red Team lead Logan Graham) rather than policy staff, and quotes Speaker Julie Menin doubting AI self-regulation.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: The man who got Anthropic banned from federal systems is now their White House ...

entry.title:

If you believe superint...

entry.title: Social Summary: October 05, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion today centered on open-model economics, agent reliability, and benchmark integrity, with optimism about falling agent costs contrasted against a heated debate over AI-safety community influence on policy.

  • Andrej Karpathy went viral arguing most of today's AI audience onboarded within the past year, framing the field as still early
  • Yann LeCun argued cheap distillation makes open-weight models economically inevitable, and separately claimed AI progress is energizing systems neuroscience research
  • Harrison Chase (LangChain) reported coding agent costs falling for a second straight month, with practical tracking and routing advice
  • Artificial Analysis debunked fake benchmark scores circulating under its name, reinforcing criticism of benchmaxxed models
  • An Anthropic product engineer admitted Claude Code's UI was not built for how good Opus is at long-running agent work
  • François Chollet countered adoption skepticism with data: ~65% of US adults use generative AI several times weekly
  • Timnit Gebru led a contentious thread alleging coordinated influence by the rationalist/AI-safety scene, including claims about Bernie Sanders's AI bills and FLI — strong reactions, unverified allegations
  • Practitioners shared hands-on value: David Ha announced a Sakana AI Tokyo symposium featuring Schmidhuber, while demo posts showcased frontier coding capability
entry.content:
Discussion today centered on open-model economics, agent reliability, and benchmark integrity, with optimism about falling agent costs contrasted against a heated debate over AI-safety community influence on policy.

  • Andrej Karpathy went viral arguing most of today's AI audience onboarded within the past year, framing the field as still early
  • Yann LeCun argued cheap distillation makes open-weight models economically inevitable, and separately claimed AI progress is energizing systems neuroscience research
  • Harrison Chase (LangChain) reported coding agent costs falling for a second straight month, with practical tracking and routing advice
  • Artificial Analysis debunked fake benchmark scores circulating under its name, reinforcing criticism of benchmaxxed models
  • An Anthropic product engineer admitted Claude Code's UI was not built for how good Opus is at long-running agent work
  • François Chollet countered adoption skepticism with data: ~65% of US adults use generative AI several times weekly
  • Timnit Gebru led a contentious thread alleging coordinated influence by the rationalist/AI-safety scene, including claims about Bernie Sanders's AI bills and FLI — strong reactions, unverified allegations
  • Practitioners shared hands-on value: David Ha announced a Sakana AI Tokyo symposium featuring Schmidhuber, while demo posts showcased frontier coding capability

entry.title: @omarsar0 My mental model for what is happening is that 99%+ of people who are now paying attention ...
entry.summary: Andrej Karpathy offers a mental model of the current AI moment: over 99% of people now paying attention to AI were onboarded within the past year, which he notes is disorienting for long-time practitioners he calls AI dinosaurs.

Yann LeCun lays out an economic argument that because training frontier models is expensive while distilling them is cheap, market forces alone will push frontier foundation models toward being free and open, citing additional supporting factors.

entry.title:
we're seeing our coding agent costs decrease significantly for second month in row
longer blog on t...
entry.summary: Harrison Chase (LangChain) reports coding agent costs dropping for a second straight month and outlines three steps: cost tracking via LangSmith, user-level cost caps through an LLM gateway, and optimizing their open-source OpenSWE harness with model routing.

entry.title: Recently learned that Schmidhuber’s Formal Theory of Fun and Creativity, covering compression progre...
entry.summary: Hardmaru highlights that Schmidhuber's Formal Theory of Fun and Creativity, framing compression progress as the basis for beauty, curiosity, art, science, music, and jokes, was published in a Japanese scientific journal in 2009, calling it wild that the framework was laid out in full formal detail 15 years ago.

entry.title: @agnesai_sapiens These are not official Artificial Analysis results. Several of these benchmarks, i...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis officially debunks circulating scores attributed to them, stating that benchmarks like AA-Briefcase and AA-Omniscience use private datasets, so the posted scores and Intelligence Index figure cannot be valid.

entry.title: @ShahabBakht I feel like the progress of AI is actually making systems neuroscience more exciting. ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun argues AI progress is making systems neuroscience more exciting: current AI lacks good angles on physical intuition, common sense, world models, planning, and motivations, but we may now have tools to implement and test cognitive architectures.

entry.title: @thiojoe When we designed the spinner, we didn’t plan for Opus becoming this good at long running wo...

This is first-party insight into agentic coding sessions now running for extremely long durations.

entry.title: there's a critical difference between benchmaxxed models and ones made by people who truly care abou...
entry.summary: CompleteSkeptic argues there is a critical difference between benchmaxxed models and models built by teams that genuinely care about reliability, a quality gap that by definition cannot show up on benchmarks, adding that the field has somewhat learned this for string-handling LLMs.

entry.title: if you’re building an ai app, you might want to host inference to improve your margins, and if you d...
entry.summary: @yoheinakajima outlines a common drift in AI app development: hosting inference to improve margins leads to supporting multiple models, which leads to building a router, then tracing and evals — concluding that this convergence explains why everyone ends up building the same AI infrastructure product.

entry.title: p(spark) is the probability that AI becomes fully creative. Fully creative means that AI makes new i...

Held at Hitotsubashi Hall with limited seating and required registration.
